data.narrative:
Nascent Materials is a Seed-stage climate and energy company founded by Chaitanya Sharma that has raised $2.3M to date. The relevant peer universe consists of nine private companies in the Climate & Energy sector, including Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen, alongside one public comparable (LNZA). A meaningful peer-median analysis proved infeasible due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables meeting minimum thresholds; only one valuation method was therefore applicable.

The Stage-Progression method uses the company's $2.3M total raised as a valuation proxy and applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage transitions, yielding an implied valuation of $5.75M. This represents a straightforward use of observed progression patterns across the venture stage spectrum and anchors directly to deployed capital.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $5M to $7M, with a median of $6M. This narrow range reflects reliance on a single triangulation method rather than independent corroboration across approaches. Key uncertainties include the absence of sufficiently comparable Seed-stage peers in the Climate & Energy sector to validate the stage-progression multiple, and the limited information on Nascent Materials' technical progress, IP position, or market traction relative to other sector participants. Gathering additional same-stage or near-stage comparable data would materially improve conviction in this range.
